channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Swiss Franc holds onto losses below 0.8100 amid firm Fed interest rate hike bets
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) holds onto Monday’s losses around 0.8088 against the US Dollar (USD) during the Asian trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls despite improved S&P Global PMI data
item.description: AUD/USD extends its losses for the sixth consecutive day, trading around 0.6980 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair remains subdued despite the release of improved preliminary Australian S&P Global Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data.

item.title: 101: United States Dollar Index remains close to 13-month highs
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, remains steady after registering modest gains in the previous day and is hovering around 101.00 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand softens to near 0.5700 despite US-Iran peace progress
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades in negative territory for the fifth consecutive day around 0.5705 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on a hawkish tone from the US Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: Japan’s Kihara says will take appropriate action against FX moves if needed
item.description: Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said that he will take appropriate action against the foreign exchang (FX) moves if needed, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hangs near April 2025 lows vs USD amid bearish oil, BoC-Fed divergence
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts some dip-buyers following the previous day's modest pullback from its highest level since April 2025 and trades around the 1.4165-1.4170 region during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD slips to near $64.50 due to hawkish Fed stance
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) loses over 1% after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $64.50 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The non-yielding Silver struggles amid a hawkish policy outlook at the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: British Pound weakens below 1.3250 as UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigns
item.description: The GBP/USD pair loses ground to near 1.3245 during the early Asian trading hours on Tuesday. Political uncertainty in the United Kingdom (UK) continues to weigh on the British Pound (GBP) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: WTI seems vulnerable near $74.00 as US lifts Iran oil sanctions amid encouraging talks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – stalls the previous day's decline and consolidates around the $74.00/barrel mark during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama reaffirms market coordination with US Treasury Secretary Bessent
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said that she held virtual talks with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday, discussing global financial markets and Iran conflict effects.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8171 vs. 6.8150 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.8171 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8150 and 6.7762 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro moves little amid market caution on ongoing US-Iran talks
item.description: EUR/USD steadies after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 1.1430 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: US VP Vance says talks between US and Iran had made “very good progress”
item.description: US Vice President (VP) JD Vance said that talks between the United States (US) and Iran have made “great progress” despite “threatening” and “whining,” CNBC reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen flatlines near 161.50 as traders are on high alert for intervention
item.description: The USD/JPY pair holds steady near 161.55 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. Progress in US–Iran peace talks and intervention fears from the Japanese authorities might cap the upside for the pair.

item.title: Gold holds steady near $4,200 as US–Iran peace progress offset by Fed hawkish stance
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades on a flat note near $4,190 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal steadies as traders continue to assess the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace deal.

item.title: Australian Dollar slips below 0.7000 as Fed repricing lifts USD
item.description: The Australian Dollar retreated by 0.15% on Monday as the US Dollar held onto gains of 0.24% in the US Dollar Index (DXY), following the round of talks between the US and Iran in Switzerland. At the time of writing, the AUD/USD tumbles below 0.7000, poised to re-test lower prices.

item.title: Australia's S&P Global Manufacturing PMI rises in June: What 51.2 means for AUD/USD
item.description: The preliminary reading of Australia's S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) rose to 51.2 in June versus 50.7 prior, the latest data published by S&P Global showed on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro falls as USD gains on Iran optimism, Lagarde tempers ECB hawks
item.description: The shared currency registered losses of 0.37% against the US Dollar on Monday late in the North American session amid positive news on the US-Iran talks, while comments from ECB President Lagarde surprised investors, who played down second-round inflation woes.

item.title: Pound Sterling braces for a heavy week as Westminster empties out
item.description: The British Pound enters the new week on the back foot, having come within a whisker of fresh seven-month lows before steadying into a tentative bounce that has done little to change the bigger picture.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar grinds lower as the Iran truce frays
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar closed lower for a fourth consecutive session on Monday, drifting toward the 0.5700 handle as a firmer US Dollar and souring risk sentiment did the damage.

item.title: New Zealand falls as a stronger US Dollar weighs on risk-sensitive currencies
item.description: The NZD/USD pair traded lower on Monday, hovering near a two-month low at the 0.5720 area, as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) came under pressure from a firmer US Dollar (USD) and cautious market sentiment.

item.title: Trump and Iran cannot agree on what they just signed
item.description: The 60-day framework that Trump and Iran's president signed at Versailles on June 17 was meant to wind the war down and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. A week on, the two capitals cannot agree on what the document actually says.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar surges near recent highs as markets watch PCE inflation and Middle East
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) traded near the 101.00 level on a positive note on Monday, near the 13-month high of 101.13 reached on Friday, as investors balanced softer Oil prices, renewed hopes for peace between the United States (US) and Iran, and expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could remain re

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens vs Dollar, Euro as SNB gets relief
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) loses ground against the US Dollar (USD) and the Euro (EUR) on Monday as risk appetite improves amid the start of US-Iran talks, which US Vice President JD Vance deemed positive.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Stays pressured against US Dollar as trades cautiously – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Malaysian Ringgit (MYR) has softened despite supportive domestic data, as Fed-led hawkish repricing keeps US Treasury yields and the US Dollar (USD) firm. Softer Oil offers only a buffer rather than a catalyst.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rises, remains supported near 101.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the Greenback against a basket of major currencies, is trading near the 101.00 area on Monday, up 0.26% on the day at the time of writing.

item.title: Mexican Peso weakens as Fed repricing lifts US Dollar ahead of Banxico
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) posts a 0.34% loss on Monday as the Greenback recovers some ground, driven by the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish tilt, which pushed the US Dollar (USD) higher. At the time of writing, USD/MXN trades at 17.35 after bouncing off daily lows of 17.30.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Bears defend 50-day SMA as intervention risks linger
item.description: AUD/JPY extends its sideways price action on Monday near levels last seen in September 1990, as persistent weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY) keeps the cross supported while fears of another intervention by Japanese authorities limit further gains.

item.title: Chinese Yuan : Testing 6.8000 within broader range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that USD/CNH spiked to 6.7980 before reversing, leaving the pair broadly unchanged near 6.78.

item.title: For the Canadian Dollar, the trade war beats the data
item.description: A hot inflation print and a rebound in Crude Oil ought to be a recipe for a stronger commodity currency, which makes the Canadian Dollar's slide to fresh 14-month lows all the more telling.
